answer: PoA resists Sybils with one-time admission proof-of-work. Each new identity pulls a single-use, expiring challenge and mines a nonce until sha256(challenge:nonce) shows the required leading zero bits; the proof is spent once, and the target bits climb whenever many joins arrive together. So an attacker posing as a lagoon scout, a glacier surveyor, or a ferrous ore trader still pays roughly N times the hashing work for N fake heads, burst joins get pricier, and rewards vest over ~25 epochs so a farm cannot cash out fast.
